question: Which of the following solutions will contain the highest concentration of {H}^+ ions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Solution with pH 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **pH scale** measures the concentration of **H⁺ ions** (protons) in a solution, ranging from 0 to 14, where **lower pH values indicate higher H⁺ ion concentrations.**
 
• A solution with a **pH of 3** is highly acidic compared to other options provided, meaning it contains the **highest concentration of H⁺ ions**.
 
• For every unit decrease in pH, the concentration of H⁺ ions increases by a factor of **10 (logarithmic scale).** Therefore, a solution with pH 3 has 10,000 times more H⁺ ions than a solution with pH 7.
 
• Solutions with **pH values of 10 and 13** are basic, meaning they have lower concentrations of H⁺ ions compared to neutral (pH 7) or acidic (pH 3) solutions.
